body:
The PCG implicit free surface fails on its first iteration with `DiagonallyDominantInversePreconditioner`: `diagonally_dominant_inverse_precondition!` returns `nothing`, which the conjugate-gradient iteration passes to `dot!` (broken since #3802). Its kernel also read the residual at `k = 1` instead of the surface index `k = Nz + 1`, outside the windowed field.

- `diagonally_dominant_inverse_precondition!` returns `P_r` and reads `r[i, j, grid.Nz+1]`.
- `test/hydrostatic_free_surface/implicit_solver.jl` runs the existing PCG solution check with this preconditioner on its three grids.

```julia
using Oceananigans
using Oceananigans.Models.HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModels: DiagonallyDominantInversePreconditioner

grid = RectilinearGrid(size=(16, 16, 4), extent=(1e5, 1e5, 1e3))
free_surface = ImplicitFreeSurface(solver_method=:PreconditionedConjugateGradient,
                                   preconditioner=DiagonallyDominantInversePreconditioner())
model = HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel(grid; free_surface)
set!(model, u=(x, y, z) -> sin(2π * x / 1e5))
time_step!(model, 1) # MethodError: no method matching dot!(::Vector{Float64}, ::Nothing, ::Field{...})
```

Closes #6191.

body:
On the fold rank of a distributed `FaceFolded` `TripolarGrid`, `worksize(grid)` is `(Nx, Ny+1, Nz)` (`DRFTRG` in `distributed_tripolar_grid.jl`), because `v` has a prognostic row at `j = Ny+1`. But `build_active_cells_map` for `AsynchronousDistributed` grids builds its regions from `size(grid)`. So the fold row is in none of the halo-independent or halo-dependent maps, and its momentum tendencies are never computed when `active_cells_map = true`. Without an active cells map, `interior_tendency_kernel_parameters` already uses `worksize`, so the fold row is covered.

We found this in a 1° ocean–sea-ice run (`FaceFolded`, `FPivot`, immersed bathymetry with `active_cells_map = true`, `Partition(1, 4)`). Serial and 4-rank runs differed at the fold row from the first step, and the 4-rank run went to NaN after about 100 steps.

### This PR
1. **Fix:** use `Utils.worksize(grid)` instead of `size(grid)` in `build_active_cells_map` for asynchronous distributed grids.
2. **Test:** the existing serial-vs-distributed tripolar simulation test, rerun with `active_cells_map = true` on `Partition(1, 4)` and `Partition(2, 2)` for all three fold topologies. The current tests never build an active cells map, so they miss this.

3. **Comment:** replace the `TODO` in `right_face_folded_kernel_parameters.jl` about buffers on asynchronous distributed `RFTRG`. The buffer kernel parameters already use `worksize` (since #5439), and this PR fixes the active cells maps.

Related: #6476 (the fold rank loses the immersed boundary condition).

body:
Fixes #6504 and therefore also NoraLoose/PanArcticShenanigans#44.

`fill_halo_regions!(fts)` for an in-memory `FieldTimeSeries` fills the halos inside `asyncmap`, which means it opens a separate Julia task. On GPU each task receives its own stream, so the halo kernels can run before the kernels that write the interior have finished, which can lead to halos being filled with old data.

This PR fixes it by running the fill halos in a loop instead of `asyncmap`. With this, two runs stay bit-identical and comparable in speed.
title: Fill FieldTimeSeries halos in a loop instead of asyncmap
